answer: An agent economy can bar sybils the way a borescope bars engine cracks: each agent gets a unique, physically bound credential seeded at hardware birth, like the tundra's permafrost layers locking identity into a fixed stratum. A challenge probe then whisper-checks micro-timing and sensor drift signatures inside that sealed identity, so cloning costs a full hardware rebuild per fake agent. The saffron-tinted limit: shared-firmware fleets can still forge near-identical signatures, capping resistance at hardware diversity.
